question: Does local Fisher natural-gradient optimization provide parameter-recovery, held-out likelihood, or optimization-cost benefit beyond strong conventional curvature-aware optimization for a fixed-variance Gaussian likelihood over the exact two-layer EBM?
hypothesis: If Fisher geometry contributes an optimization advantage beyond generic local curvature on this task, the preregistered local-Fisher natural-gradient method should improve held-out likelihood, log-parameter recovery, or residual-evaluation cost without reducing convergence relative to SciPy Jacobian-scaled trust-region least squares. Equivalent outcomes do not establish a uniquely information-geometric benefit because the local Fisher step equals Gauss-Newton for this likelihood.

datasets.quality_control_policy: literature-fixed positive finite reference parameters; truth is used only to generate synthetic observations and score recovery

datasets.time_domain: step and ramp discovery histories with separately held-out nonmonotone confirmation histories
datasets.quality_control_policy: protocol identities and forcing histories are immutable; confirmation protocols are never used in fitting

datasets.time_domain: four fresh synthetic observation realizations crossed with four frozen optimizer starts
datasets.quality_control_policy: all seeds, starts, bounds, optimizer tolerances, pairing, confirmation thresholds, and interpretation rules were committed before confirmation execution

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: local Fisher natural-gradient step versus ordinary least-squares Gauss-Newton step at the frozen optimizer starts on the first fresh discovery dataset
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: all four frozen starts require finite full-rank Jacobians
primary_metrics.uncertainty_method: deterministic numerical identity witness under the fixed Gaussian likelihood

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: median across the 16 matched fresh seed/start trials on held-out overshoot/reversal and sign-reversal forcing histories
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: all 16 matched trials are required; optimizer nonconvergence remains part of method diagnostics rather than dropping the trial

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: median recovery error difference across the 16 matched fresh seed/start trials
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: all four parameter coordinates and all 16 trials are required

secondary_metrics.aggregation_domain: median method-reported standardized-residual evaluation count across 16 matched trials
secondary_metrics.missing_data_policy: all method trials are required; counts are interpreted only within this fixed executor

secondary_metrics.aggregation_domain: preregistered interpretation rule comparing candidate outcome, convergence, and cost against the primary TRF comparator
secondary_metrics.missing_data_policy: all primary comparison fields are required

negative_controls: freeze the Fisher matrix at initialization while retaining the same observations, bounds, Armijo policy, and optimization budget
compare against SciPy Jacobian-scaled trust-region least squares using the same full local centered log-parameter Jacobian rather than only against raw gradient descent
compare against SciPy L-BFGS-B with the same exact centered-sensitivity gradient and common log-parameter bounds
use held-out overshoot/reversal and sign-reversal forcing histories only for confirmation scoring and never for parameter fitting
falsifiers: the local Fisher and ordinary Gauss-Newton steps disagree beyond the preregistered 1e-10 relative tolerance
the natural-gradient candidate has lower convergence than the primary TRF comparator without a compensating preregistered held-out likelihood or recovery improvement
natural gradient and TRF have equivalent held-out likelihood and recovery within preregistered tolerances while natural gradient does not use fewer residual evaluations
the frozen-Fisher negative control is treated as the primary conventional baseline
a matched or weaker result is nevertheless described as evidence for a Fisher-specific optimization advantage
split_policy: Fit only noisy temperatures from held_out_step and held_out_ramp. Score recovery and likelihood on overshoot_reversal and sign_reversal, which remain unavailable to every optimizer during fitting. Four fresh dataset seeds are crossed with four preregistered log-parameter starts for 16 matched trials.
preprocessing: Use both EBM temperature-state coordinates in kelvin anomaly. Add fixture-seeded independent Gaussian noise with fixed known standard deviation 0.05 K. Optimize four positive parameters in log coordinates under identical bounds. Use the existing centered log-parameter sensitivity route with fixed step 1e-4.
stopping_rule: Execute exactly the 16 seed/start combinations and all four registered methods under frozen budgets. Report every trial, convergence status, held-out likelihood, log-parameter recovery, residual/Jacobian evaluation counts, and the Gauss-Newton equivalence witness. Do not retune starts, seeds, bounds, tolerances, or interpretation thresholds after execution.
multiple_comparison_policy: The primary comparison is local Fisher natural gradient versus SciPy Jacobian-scaled TRF. L-BFGS-B and frozen-initial-Fisher are secondary baseline/negative-control diagnostics and cannot replace the primary comparator after seeing results.
